summary: letI providing a bundled-data instance (e.g. NormedSpace K L, which extends Module K L) must become `let :`, NOT plain `have :` — an anonymous `have` makes the instance opaque and desyncs the bundled Module from the Algebra-induced one, breaking a later `rcases`/elaboration via an instance diamond. The style rule 'prefer have over haveI/letI' holds for Prop-only instances; for a class that bundles data, drop the I to `let` (keeps the value transparent) rather than `have`.

`isUnit_map_iff` (with `algebraMap K L` auto-synthesized as IsLocalHom for a field hom) replaces hand-rolled `isUnit_iff_ne_zero`/`fun h0 ↦ …` unit-reflection across a coefficient map; `simp only [PowerSeries.coeff_map, isUnit_map_iff]` discharges `IsUnit (coeff k (map φ f)) ↔ IsUnit (coeff k f)`.

The mathlib-search step (audit item 13 / Phase 5a) MUST grep the project's own ForMathlib/*.lean files, not only .lake/packages/mathlib. In a project whose ForMathlib tree REPLACES upstream mathlib files, the general lemma often already lives there. Here `isRestricted_mapAlgebra` was a thin wrapper (isometry over algebraMap) whose more-general form `PowerSeries.isRestricted_map` (contraction ≤ over any φ : R →+* S) already existed in the project's Restricted/Basic.lean; the worker's mathlib-only grep missed it and wrongly concluded 'not in mathlib, keep local'. Correct outcome: delete the wrapper, call isRestricted_map c (fun x ↦ (hiso x).le) f.2 directly.

pattern: Codepoint vs byte line-length: a byte-based `awk length>100` scan on Lean files rich in ‖ ≥ ℝ ∈ ↦ glyphs massively over-reports long lines. mathlib's longLine linter counts Unicode codepoints. Measure with Python len() on the decoded line (or trust a warning-free `lake env lean`), not `wc -c`/awk bytes, before flagging or reflowing.

Per-declaration golf workers verify via `lake build <module>` + `lake env lean <file>` (the latter runs ALL frontend linters incl. unusedSectionVars, zero output = clean) because the mcp__lean-lsp__* tools are NOT exposed to subagents in this session. `lake env lean <file>` is robust to a concurrent instance rebuilding UPSTREAM files, whereas `lake build` transiently fails on the neighbour's in-progress edits — distinguish 'failure in a file I didn't edit' (neighbour) from a real regression.

pattern: Extracting a helper lemma from inside a section commonly trips the unusedSectionVars linter (e.g. NormMulClass/CompleteSpace unused by the helper). This file's convention is to prepend the exact `omit [...] in` the linter suggests — matching the many existing `omit [NormMulClass R] in` / `omit [CompleteSpace R] in` prefixes. Always re-run `lake env lean <file>` after an extraction to catch it.

lesson: When extracting a helper lemma from a proof body, instance hypotheses that were satisfied by a local `have` in the parent (e.g. `have hntR : Nontrivial R := hg.nontrivial`) do NOT travel with the extracted code — they must be re-derived inside the new helper. Symptoms: `failed to synthesize Nontrivial R` at the exact site using `Monic.ne_zero` / `Monic.coeff_natDegree`. Fix: add the `have hntR : Nontrivial R := hg.nontrivial` line to each helper. Also run the unusedSectionVars linter afterward and extend the helper`s `omit [...]` clause (e.g. drop `NormOneClass R`) for whatever the extracted subset no longer uses.

pattern: For AddMonoidAlgebra R M (incl. LaurentPolynomial R = R[T;T-1]), pointwise coeff-of-ring-op lemmas are definitional: (p + q).coeff m = p.coeff m + p.coeff m := rfl and likewise for sub, since AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff_add/coeff_sub and Finsupp.add_apply/sub_apply are each rfl. In an ultrametric normed (add) group, to prove norm (a + b) = norm a when norm b < norm a, use IsUltrametricDist.norm_add_eq_max_of_norm_ne_norm (the isosceles-triangle lemma, additive via to_additive; note the IsUltrametricDist namespace) giving norm (a+b) = max, then max_eq_left hab.le. Units.ofNearby (u : Rˣ) (y : R) (h : ‖y - u‖ < ‖(u⁻¹ : R)‖⁻¹) : Rˣ (Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Ring.Units, needs NormedRing + HasSummableGeomSeries) constructs the unit structure of an element near a unit; its val is y definitionally (@[simps! val]/Units.copy), so (u.ofNearby y h).isUnit : IsUnit y. Replaces the whole manual geometric-series tail (t := u⁻¹(u-y); ‖t‖<1; Units.oneSub; mul_sub/ring). In a NormMulClass ring ‖(↑u⁻¹)‖⁻¹ = ‖↑u‖ so the bound is just ‖y - ↑u‖ < ‖↑u‖.

Decomposing isUnit_of_ne_zero (every nonzero elt of a Gauss extension is a unit): split along the two mathematical layers. Layer 1 (GaussLaurent, off the divisible closure): exists_isUnit_norm_sub_lt — a nonzero p is within its own norm of a unit (its dominant monomial q=single m (coeff m)), with a tail-estimate helper norm_sub_lt_of_coeff_eq_single (‖p-q‖<‖p‖ via gaussTerm injectivity). Layer 2 (completion): dense-approximate x by ofLaurent p of equal norm, lift q to a unit U near x, finish with Units.ofNearby. 103 lines → 24 (main) + 27 + 28, all <50.

The GaussLaurent Field section (the NormMulClass instance plus the dominant-monomial unit-approximation lemmas exists_isUnit_norm_sub_lt / norm_sub_lt_of_coeff_eq_single) only needs [NormedField K], NOT [NontriviallyNormedField K]: nontriviality (exists_one_lt_norm) is used only by the GaussExtension NontriviallyNormedField instance downstream, not by any GaussLaurent-level fact. Helpers extracted during /decompose-proof from a NontriviallyNormedField context routinely over-inherit — reassess the typeclass and the home file once the proof settles.

When a proof applies a coefficientwise retraction to every coefficient of a Polynomial (∑ m ∈ r.support, monomial m (⟨fun t ↦ π (coeff t (r.coeff m).1), _⟩)), bundle the per-coefficient map as a `ZeroHom` (only needs toFun + map_zero') so the generic helpers Polynomial.coeff_finsetSum_monomial_apply and Polynomial.degree_finsetSum_monomial_apply_lt apply directly. This mirrors the univariate case (where π is already a bundled LinearMap): it eliminated the hand-rolled hπT0/hr₀coeff/hr₀deg (~40 lines) in weierstrassDivision_descend_of_retraction, cutting the proof from ~80 to ~30 lines. The final coeff goal closes by `rfl` after rw, since ⇑ρ of a ZeroHom literal reduces definitionally.

pattern: Extracted MvPowerSeries.Restricted.mapRetraction : Restricted S c →+ Restricted R c — coefficientwise application of a norm-bounded additive map π : S →+ R (via isRestricted_mk), bundled as an AddMonoidHom (map_zero'/map_add' each `Subtype.ext (MvPowerSeries.ext fun t ↦ by change ...; simp)`). val_mapRetraction := rfl. Reuses across the two descend call sites (ρ at Fin.tail c, q₀ at c) and gives ZeroHomClass for Polynomial.coeff/degree_finsetSum_monomial_apply. Replaces the inline ZeroHom.

Two dead-ends when mirroring Mv→univariate: (1) A univariate PowerSeries.Restricted.mapRetraction cannot cleanly delegate to the Mv one: univariate q₀ needs the `PowerSeries.mk fun n ↦ π (coeff n A.1)` coeff form (its proof uses coeff_mk/change), but the Mv mapRetraction gives the raw `fun t ↦ π (coeff t A.1)` form, and `single () (t()) = t` is only propositional — so val_add won't fire and `change` fails. Univariate has no internal retraction duplication anyway, so leave it. (2) isDistinguishedX0_mapAlgebra cannot become an `iff` like the univariate isDistinguished_mapAlgebra_iff: the Mv unit component IsUnit(coeff s ·) lives in the coefficient RING Restricted K (Fin.tail c), not a field, so isUnit_map_iff (field unit reflection) does not apply; reverse needs Tate-algebra unit reflection (absent). (3) mapAlgebra's [IsUltrametricDist K/L] are load-bearing for the TYPE Restricted K d (defined under variable [IsUltrametricDist R]), not droppable.

summary: first-blocks with per-goal alternatives are a lint smell
detail: Using `first | tac1 | tac2 | ...` to cover several goals produced 11 `tactic does nothing` / `never executed` warnings — each block carries N-1 dead branches per goal. Once the goals are known, resolve each individually with an explicit bullet. Applies to linear_combination coefficient search in particular.
